blocks.text: In Writing in Role, students step into a character’s shoes and write as that character. It’s quick, free-flowing and judgment-free.

items.text: Share a short story with the class. In ours, we read about Wangari Maathai.
Students write non-stop for about two minutes, capturing any thoughts, worries, hopes or feelings the main character might have.
No erasing, no stopping to think about spelling, no worrying about sounding “academic.” The goal is to let the ideas flow.

blocks.text: let students know this writing is just for them. Nobody else has to read it, which frees them to be honest and take risks.
Writing in Role builds empathy and deep understanding of a text. To write as a character, students have to think like one. The short time limit keeps the energy high and the pressure low.

in our class, we did several of these strategies back-to-back, all based on the same story. Each one works on its own, but linked together they build into a rich, layered exploration of a text. Combine them for maximum impact! Writing in Role leads naturally into Group Monologue.
